# dsh-cad — CAD Plugin for DeepSeek Harness

![dsh-cad banner](docs/img/banner.svg)

[![homepage](https://img.shields.io/badge/homepage-dsh--cad-4D6BFE)](https://lau-mars.github.io/dsh-cad/)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-cad)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-cad)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-cad)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-cad)
[![dsh](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@deepseek-ai%2Fdsh?label=dsh)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D%2022-4D6BFE)](https://nodejs.org/)
[![occt](https://img.shields.io/badge/occt-7.9.3-4D6BFE)](https://github.com/LAU-MARS/opencascade-ts)
[![occt.ts](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/occt.ts?label=occt.ts)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/occt.ts)
[![ansatz](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/ansatz-wasm?label=ansatz)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ansatz-wasm)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-4D6BFE)](./LICENSE)

English | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md)

A CAD plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness):
an **embedded 3D/2D CAD viewer** plus a **native parametric modeling tool family**
(OCCT kernel) in the Web UI, letting the agent build and inspect CAD geometry
step by step — "model while you watch".

## Preview

A full modeling session, end to end: the agent builds a parametric assembly
from plain chat — a 120×80×8 base plate with R5 rounded corners, then four
bolt instances placed at the corners — while the resident CAD panel tracks
every step live (parts tree with per-instance colors, ViewCube, "装配体"
assembly tab, 5 instances · 1,740 triangles). The finished assembly exports
as a structured STEP document and the agent verifies it by reading the file
back — 2 solids, 3 products, 2 assembly usages, 1,125.00 mm³:

![dsh-cad assembly session](docs/img/assembly-preview.png)

## Downloads

Cumulative downloads from the npm registry, refreshed daily by CI:

![npm cumulative downloads](docs/img/downloads-cumulative.svg)

## Feature Overview

| Capability | Description |
| --- | --- |
| ⚙️ Single-kernel architecture | **occt.ts as the primary modeling kernel** (true B-splines, native shell/draft, centroid); opencascade.js stays only as the fallback backend; the old "no editing after shell" seam is gone — fillet/chamfer/boolean keep working after shelling |
| 🔍 CAD viewing | STL / OBJ / STEP / IGES / BREP / DCPRT (3D), DXF / SVG (2D); interactive viewport in the resident right panel (orbit / zoom / wireframe / pan), with a one-line result row in the conversation |
| 🧭 CAD editor interactions | Onshape-style ViewCube (26-zone click-to-orient), hover/click face & edge picking with live measurement (area mm² / length mm), Faces+Edges / Faces / Wireframe render modes, switchable BRep demo parts (bracket / flange / shaft) |
| 🏗️ Parametric modeling | Primitives, profile extrusion, **loft**, **sweep**, **revolve**, booleans, all-edge fillet/chamfer, **shell**, **draft**, **patterns** (linear/circular), transforms; profiles take **curve segments** (arcs/circles exact BRep; B-splines sampled approximation) — exact OCCT BRep, not a mesh approximation |
| ✏️ Named sketches | Standalone named profiles (Sketch1…) kept in the document (`cad_sketch_new` / `edit` / `list` / `delete`); extrude/revolve/sweep reference them **by name**, and `cad_sketch_edit` rewrites the definition in place + replays the log, rebuilding every dependent feature — the parametric loop. Sketches render as Onshape-style **blue curves + plane frame** in the viewport (refreshing live on edit), listed in a left-side **feature tree** (sketches + features, eye-toggle visibility, click-to-highlight bodies) over the Part tab |
| 🗂️ Codex-style document tabs | The resident display panel gets a tab strip with a "+" menu: **Part** (Part Studio, the default) / **Assembly** (instance insert/move/remove) / **Drawing** (true hidden-line sheets); tabs are closable and keep their state |
| 📁 Multi-document file space | Named documents per workspace (`.dsh-cad/docs/`), each session bound to its own active document — new sessions start empty instead of inheriting leftovers; a folder button in the panel lists every document (preview / delete), and `cad_doc_new` / `cad_doc_open` manage the modeling target from chat |
| 📐 Engineering drawings | GB first-angle layout: front / top / left views + isometric, true OCCT hidden-line removal via the **occt.ts** kernel (an npm dependency, dashed); sheet frame, title block, overall dimensions, standard scale series; exports SVG / DXF |
| 🔗 Constraint solving & motion | **Ansatz** geometric constraint solver (**one command: `npm install ansatz-wasm`** — a wasm dependency, no Rust toolchain, no native binary): entity/constraint modeling (assembly instances ↔ rigid3 poses mapped automatically), solve-with-writeback, full DOF/residual/redundancy/suggestion diagnostics (LLM-oriented), and parametric kinematic sweeps (`cad_constraint` / `cad_solve` / `cad_motion`) |
| 📐 Geometry measurement | Exact volume (mm³), bounding box, triangle counts, DXF layers |
| 📤 On-demand export | STEP (parametric) / STL (mesh); files are written only when the user asks |
| 🖥️ Resident CAD panel | A permanent panel right of the conversation: Codex-style tabs (Part / Assembly / Drawing), tracking the latest model in real time while modeling |
| ⚡ Zero-copy render pipeline | worker mesh → in-memory binary → three.js typed arrays; zero base64 / zero intermediate files / zero per-step disk writes |
| 💾 Modeling document persistence | Operation log (JSON) + debounced disk mirror; automatically replayed to restore state after a process restart |
| 🖼️ Image → profile | PNG sketch/screenshot → Otsu binarization → contour tracing → extrusion-ready polygon (`cad_image_profile`) |
| 🔌 FreeCAD executor | Run the same op family on an external FreeCAD console (STEP in/out); requires a local FreeCAD install |
| ☁️ Onshape executor | Run the same op family on **Onshape** over its signed REST API — zero local install; every op compiles to a **standard Onshape feature** pushed into the target Part Studio (no Feature Studio setup). Readback is three-tier: cheap per-part STL by default, `readback: "step"` for exact-BRep-derived named meshes via a server-side STEP translation, or `readback: "none"` — build only and return the document link (~3 calls, quota-friendliest). Exports `.stl` / `.step` / `.x_t` (Parasolid). Quota-aware errors distinguish credential problems from free-plan cooldowns; the Onshape document URL is always surfaced |

## Installation

The plugin is published to npm — one line:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cad
```

The installer applies the bundled `cordis.patch.yml` (declared in the `dsh.bundle` manifest) automatically, so there is nothing to configure by hand.

### Version requirements

- **Node.js** and **dsh CLI** (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`): minimum versions live in
  the badge row above and the `engines` field of `package.json` — kept out of
  the prose so they never go stale

### Install from source (dev mode)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LAU-MARS/dsh-cad.git
cd dsh-cad
npm install && npm run build && npm test   # deps include occt.ts (true-HLR drawing kernel, ~20MB wasm)

npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh pnpm
dsh web                                  # let the first launch init the profile, then Ctrl-C

dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-cad

dsh web
```

The patch insert ships as `cordis.patch.yml` in the package root and is applied by the installer via the same `dsh.bundle` manifest.

Set `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and you are ready — for example:

- “open bracket.stl” → `cad_view`
- “model a 100×60×5 plate, punch a ⌀20 hole in the middle, R2 fillets on the four
  corners, add a ⌀16 boss 20 tall, export plate.step”
  → `cad_create_prim` + `cad_boolean` + `cad_fillet` + `cad_export`, with the 3D tab
  updating live at every step
- “build a snowman” → spheres + a cone nose + a cylinder hat (precise `at`/`axis` placement)
- “add two more b1, one rotated 90 degrees” → `cad_assembly_insert` + `cad_assembly_move`, the Assembly tab updates live
- “make an A3 drawing of b1 and export dxf” → `cad_drawing` (three views + iso + dashed hidden lines + dimensions) → `cad_export` `.dxf`

## Modeling Tool Family

| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `cad_view` | Open a CAD file and render it in the viewer (resident panel) |
| `cad_info` | Read-only geometry metadata (format / counts / bounding box / units / layers) |
| `cad_create_prim` | Primitives (mm, Z-up); `at` for placement, `axis` for orientation (exact axis-angle rotation) |
| `cad_sketch_new` | Create a named sketch (Sketch1…): {start, segments} / {circle} / flat points loop — referenced by name from the profile features |
| `cad_sketch_edit` | Redefine a sketch (回改): the definition op is rewritten in place and the log replayed — every referencing feature rebuilds |
| `cad_sketch_list` | List the document's sketches (name / form / size) |
| `cad_sketch_delete` | Delete a sketch (refused while features still reference it) |
| `cad_extrude_profile` | Extrude a closed XY-plane profile along +Z into a solid — inline points/segments/circle or a named sketch (`sketch`) |
| `cad_loft` | Loft: skin a solid through successive closed sections (each a [x,y,z,…] loop in its own plane); sections may differ in shape and point count; `ruled` for straight sides |
| `cad_revolve` | Solid of revolution: revolve a closed profile around an axis (profile coords = (radius, height); curve segments supported — rounded rims exact); optional `angle`; accepts a named sketch |
| `cad_chamfer` | Chamfer: bevel every sharp edge with one equal distance (mm) |
| `cad_pattern` | Pattern: linear (`delta` spacing) or circular (principal axis + `at` point + sweep angle); creates copy bodies, fuse afterwards for one body |
| `cad_shell` | Shell: hollow to a wall thickness (inward, outer skin preserved); `open` lists outward normals of the faces to open (empty = sealed). Runs on the occt.ts kernel; the result is a HOSTED body |
| `cad_draft` | Draft: tilt the walls `angle` degrees about a neutral plane (mold release); `direction` is the pull direction, walls auto-selected by default. Runs on the occt.ts kernel; the result is a HOSTED body |
| `cad_sweep` | Sweep: pipe a closed 2D profile along a 3D [x,y,z,…] path; the profile is auto-placed on the start plane, so no manual orientation; accepts a named sketch |
| `cad_boolean` | fuse / cut / common (classic hole punching: plate cut cylinder) |
| `cad_fillet` | Constant-radius fillet on all sharp edges |
| `cad_transform` | Translate / Euler rotate / mirror |
| `cad_volume` | Exact BRep volume (mm³) |
| `cad_drawing` | Engineering drawing: front/top/left + isometric views, dashed hidden lines, frame, title block, overall dimensions, standard scale, A4/A3 |
| `cad_assembly_insert` | Insert a body into the assembly as a placed instance (`at` position, `rotate` orientation) |
| `cad_assembly_move` | Set an instance's absolute placement |
| `cad_assembly_remove` | Remove an instance from the assembly (the body stays) |
| `cad_constraint` | Declare the constraint model: entities (assembly-instance bindings) + constraints (distance/angle/mate/coaxial…), persisted in the op log |
| `cad_solve` | Solve with Ansatz and write poses back; returns DOF/residual/redundancy/suggestion diagnostics |
| `cad_motion` | Kinematic sweep: drive one constraint value from `from` to `to`, solve frame by frame, apply the last pose, return the motion table |
| `cad_export` | Export STEP / STL / DCPRT (the native replayable part document) to a workspace path; `target: "assembly"` writes the assembly STEP, `target: "drawing"` writes the sheet as SVG / DXF |
| `cad_delete` | Delete a body |
| `cad_docs` | List the workspace's modeling documents (id / name / bodies / updated, active marked) |
| `cad_doc_new` | Create a named document and make it the session's modeling target (start multi-part projects here) |
| `cad_doc_open` | Open an existing document (by id or name) as the session's modeling target — bodies replay exactly |
| `cad_doc_rename` | Rename a document |
| `cad_doc_delete` | Permanently delete a document (requires `confirm: true`) |
| `cad_freecad` | Run an op program on an external FreeCAD executor (optional STEP input / export) |
| `cad_fusion` | Run an op program on an external Fusion 360 executor (GUI bridge; optional export) |
| `cad_onshape` | Run an op program on the Onshape cloud (signed REST API): creates or drives a document, returns its URL; `readback: "step"` for exact BRep meshes; exports `.stl` / `.step` / `.x_t` (Parasolid) |
| `cad_image_profile` | PNG → contours → extrusion-ready polygon points |
| `cad_script` | Deterministic script evaluation for geometry math (profile point arrays, arc coordinates): `js` runs in-process (Node vm — works even when the host shell is unavailable), `py` uses a system Python |

After every modeling step: **the chat result row updates in place** (stable viewId +
versioned URL), and the resident panel's "Part" tab tracks the latest model in real time.

## Connectors (roadmap)

Modeling primarily runs on the **occt.ts kernel** (opencascade.js as the fallback backend) (OCCT in the browser —
zero install). The connectors below refer to **external CAD engines** acting as
executors for the same tool family, planned for future support:

| Connector | Suite | Platform | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Built-in kernel** | CAD modeling kernel based on OCCT + WebGL, runs in the browser — zero install | All platforms (WebGL rendering) | ✅ Built-in |
| FreeCAD | open-source parametric suite — natural local executor via its Python API (console + GUI window modes) | Windows / macOS / Linux | ✅ Available (needs local install) |
| Fusion 360 | Autodesk CAD/CAM — resident add-in + spool bridge (no headless; the Fusion window doubles as a viewer) | Windows / macOS | 🧪 Experimental (`cad_fusion`) |
| SolidWorks | Dassault Systèmes industry-standard 3D CAD, COM/.NET automation | Windows only | 🚧 Windows demo scaffold (`scripts/solidworks-bridge/`) |
| Onshape | PTC cloud-native SaaS CAD, fully in the browser — signed REST API (cad.onshape.com or chamber hosts); every op compiles to a standard Onshape feature pushed into the Part Studio, results read back as per-part STL + mass properties, the cloud is the viewer | All platforms (browser) | ✅ Available (`cad_onshape`; set `DSH_ONSHAPE_ACCESS_KEY` / `DSH_ONSHAPE_SECRET_KEY`) |
| ZW3D（中望3D） | ZWSOFT all-in-one CAD/CAM | Windows / Linux | 🚧 Planned |
| GstarCAD 3D（浩辰3D） | Gstarsoft 3D CAD | Windows | 🚧 Planned |

All external engines implement the same **GeometryExecutor contract** (`available()` /
`run(opProgram) → meshes`), so the WebGL display layer never changes — swapping a
backend changes only the quality of the produced geometry.

## Architecture

```
cad_view(path)                        modeling tools (cad_create_prim, …)
  → import worker (occt-import-js)      → modeling worker (opencascade.js WASM)
  → CadScene JSON (base64-f32)          → exact BRep geometry + meshing
  → GET /dsh-cad/scene/<id>            → in-memory binary scene (f32/u32 packed)
                                        → GET /dsh-cad/bin/<docId>
            ↓ session presentationMeta (viewId + versioned URL) ↓
        browser card + persistent "3D" tab (three.js / SVG, Z-up, XYZ axes)
```

- **Two workers**: import (occt-import-js, read-only STEP/IGES/BREP) and modeling
  (opencascade.js, full OCCT) are separate, both lazily started; the `_N`
  suffix convention of embind overloaded constructors is wrapped in
  `src/modeling/occt-adapter.cjs` (all verified at runtime)
- **Zero-copy pipeline**: modeling scenes use zero base64 / zero large JSON arrays /
  zero per-step disk writes (disk mirror debounced 1.5s, replayed only on service
  restart); `cad_export` is the only explicit file export
- **Modeling document**: `<workspace>/.dsh-cad/model.json` operation log; all bodies
  are restored by replay after a restart
- **Drawing HLR kernel**: hidden lines run on **occt.ts** (npm dependency,
  `npm i occt.ts`) — true OCCT removal, no fallback engine, a missing kernel is
  a hard error. New APIs over opencascade.js: `hiddenLines()` true hidden-line
  removal, byte-level STEP/BRep `readStep`/`readBrep`/`writeStep`/`writeBrep`
  without MEMFS, tessellation with built-in feature-edge extraction, and a
  `hasError()`/`lastError()` error contract. Geometry crosses kernels as STEP
  bytes and the projected segments are remapped into the sheet frame. Kernel
  dist resolution: `DSH_OCCTJS_DIST` env var → Node's own resolution of the
  `occt.ts` dependency (walks up every parent node_modules — npm/yarn flat and
  pnpm symlink layouts all hit) → `<repo>/../opencascade-ts/dist` (sibling
  checkout) → `vendor/` → `node_modules/opencascade-ts`
- **Constraint solving (Ansatz)**: the solver is the npm dependency
  **`ansatz-wasm`** (a wasm-bindgen build, single package ~538KB, zero deps) —
  installing dsh-cad pulls it automatically, and `npm install ansatz-wasm` alone
  upgrades it. **No Rust toolchain, no native binary, platform independent.**
  Resolution: the npm package (node_modules) → a `DSH_ANSATZ_WASM` directory → a
  sibling Ansatz checkout's pkg-node. The solver speaks one JSON envelope
  contract, with tool-layer errors (e.g. `unsupported_constraint`) surfaced
  verbatim for the LLM. Assembly placements (translate + XYZ Euler
  degrees) map bidirectionally to the solver's rigid3 poses (translate +
  exponential-map rotation, radians). Solver capability is staged
  (point-distance-to-origin today) — the plumbing contract is finished and needs
  no changes as it grows
- **Single-kernel architecture**: the primary modeling kernel is
  **occt.ts** — primitives, curve-segment profiles (TRUE B-spline
  interpolation), loft/sweep/revolve, booleans, fillet/chamfer, shell/draft,
  mirror (composed as scale(-1) + a π rotation) and centroid all live in one
  session; engineering-drawing HLR takes the shape directly (zero STEP hops);
  editing after shelling is seamless (the old hosted-body seam is deleted).
  opencascade.js remains as the FALLBACK backend (auto-selected when occt.ts
  cannot load). Assembly STEP export writes a **structured document** (occt.ts
  `writeStepDocument`): one root product plus one named, placed child
  per instance — instance separation survives the file (STL stays a single
  fused mesh; the fallback backend also fuses). Instance separation stays in
  the assembly scene/document for the fuse paths.
  Face selection matches `describe()` plane normals (outermost along ±normal)
- **Client**: esbuild single-file CJS factory (three.js inlined ~560KB, react provided
  by the host module table), Z-up CAD convention, empty scene with XYZ axis labels
  and a ground grid always displayed

## Tests

```sh
npm test                             # full suite: converters / modeling worker (exact volume assertions) / DCPRT round-trip / FreeCAD + Onshape executors / image profiles / binary pipeline / document persistence
node test/m0-kernel-check.cjs        # OCCT kernel API smoke test
node test/route-check.mjs            # JSON scene routing layer
node test/visual/serve.mjs           # browser card/tab visual verification page (http://127.0.0.1:3987)
```

Representative assertions covered: the boolean-punched volume exactly equals the
analytic value (28429.20 mm³), L-shaped profile extrusion 3000 mm³, volumes and
bounding-box flips of sphere/cone/torus placed with `at`/`axis`, 8-byte alignment
of the binary packing, an STL export round-trip (export → read back by the
phase-1 parser), and a DCPRT document round-trip (serialize → replay on the
OCCT worker → exact bounds).

## Known Limitations

- DWG (closed-source) is unsupported; DXF bulge arcs are approximated by chords;
  glTF/3MF viewing is not implemented (the structure is reserved)
- `cad_fillet` is all-edge constant-radius (per-edge selection is unstable under
  embind); chamfer is not implemented
- Sketch extrusion supports polygon profiles only (arc profiles are constructed by
  boolean combinations of cylinders/tori)
- dsh framework limitation: an already-mounted single slot (the right-side details
  panel itself) does not respond to components registered later, so the persistent
  view is provided as the "3D" view tab (a list slot, the official composition)
- The host reads CAD files via node:fs (the platform fs service supports UTF-8 text
  only and cannot carry binary data)

# DSHPlugin

English | [中文说明](README.zh.md)

A workspace for authoring plugins for the **official DeepSeek Harness desktop app**
([deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), dsh). That app is the Electron build at
`F:\Code\dsh`, its `DSH_HOME` is `~/.dsh` and its profile is `desktop`. It is the environment these plugins
are developed and verified against, and the one a phone reaches.

The plugins themselves live in the sibling repository
[LBurny/dsh-plugin](https://github.com/LBurny/dsh-plugin): one feature per package, each installed on its own
from the app's **Plugins** page (Add plugin, then paste a spec). This repository is where they are designed,
documented and tested, and where the authoring skill lives. It is not a plugin package itself.

## What lives here

- **`.agents/skills/dsh-plugin-authoring/`**: the authoring skill. `SKILL.md` states the plugin contract
  (bundle patch, `dsh.bundle.patch`, row ids, the ESM plugin module) and the install, verify and uninstall
  recipes. `references/plugin-contract.md` lists every extension point with examples taken from the runtime
  itself, and `references/repo-delivery.md` holds the sandbox and delivery recipes.
  `assets/plugin-selftest.mjs` is the module-level self-check that catches the mistakes which silently
  keep your own row from activating, and `assets/plugin-template/` is the three-file skeleton to copy.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: the environment facts (which app, which home, which profile, what resolves where) and the
  traps that are easy to get wrong.

## Retired: `dsh-desktop-kit`

Until 2026-10-10 this repository *was* a plugin package. `dsh-desktop-kit` was an all-in-one plugin that
ported the DSHDesktop desktop shell's conveniences into dsh: skill and MCP management, diagnostics, page
zoom, task reminders, shortcut rebinding, `/init`, and phone remote access. The eight packages of the sibling
repository were split out of it. The shell it was written for is a separate, older product with its own home
and its own UI, and the project now aims at the official app, so the package was removed from the working tree
along with its documentation and its test suites.

It is intact in history:

```bash
git tag --list 'archive/*'            # archive/kit-final is its last state
git show archive/kit-final --stat     # what it contained
git checkout archive/kit-final -- .   # bring it back into the working tree
```

Two of its features never made it into the split packages, in case either is ever wanted again: the `/kit`
command, and page-error reporting, where the panel's log view listed the page's own JavaScript errors.

## License

MIT.

# dsh-doctor

Harness diagnostics from inside dsh: version, port, pid, uptime, memory, profile, and a log tail.

Ported from DSHDesktop's diagnostics page. Two log sources, best effort in this order:

1. The desktop shell's unified `events.log` (`<DSH_HOME>/../events.log`), present when this dsh runs
   under DSHDesktop — that file already holds both the shell's lines and the child dsh's stdout.
2. This plugin's own ring buffer, which always exists.

A bare `~/.dsh` setup therefore still gets a useful panel.

## Placement

With **[dsh-features](../dsh-features)** (the Features hub) installed, this panel appears on that hub's single
page and no longer docks its own corner button; without the hub — a bare dsh, or a profile where it is
not installed — the floating panel is built exactly as before. The coupling is two DOM-level
conventions (`window.__dshFeatures`, `#dsh-launchers`), described in the repository's AGENTS.md.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-doctor
# pin a commit:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#<sha>&path:/dsh-doctor
```

`--profile web` = DSHDesktop's shell, `--profile desktop` = the official desktop app; the panel needs no flag.

Restart dsh afterwards — plugins have no HMR.

## What it does

- **Status**: dsh and node versions, state, port, pid, uptime, resident memory, profile name, DSH
  home, patch document path, session count, platform.
- **Log tail**: the last 500 lines of the shell log (read through a 512 KB byte window, with the
  partial first line dropped) or of the plugin's own ring.
- **`/doctor`** prints a compact version of the same thing, ten log lines included.

## Routes

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| ------ | ---- | ------- |
| GET | `/dsh-doctor/panel.js` `/dsh-doctor/panel.css` | browser half |
| GET | `/dsh-doctor/api/diagnostics` | the status document |
| GET | `/dsh-doctor/api/logs` | `{ source, path, lines }` |

## Data

Nothing. This plugin writes no files and edits no configuration; it only reads.

## Caveats

- It cannot **restart** dsh: the plugin runs inside the process being restarted. Use the desktop
  shell's tray menu, or your own process manager.
- It reports only its own plugin's actions in the ring. Other `dsh-plugin` packages keep their own
  logs; the shared `events.log` is the place to see everything at once.

## Test

```bash
cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/plugins/dsh-doctor"
node tests/doctor.test.mjs
```

## License

MIT.

# dsh-plugin

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Small independent [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) plugins: one feature per package, each installable on its own. Ported out of [DSHDesktop](https://github.com/LBurny/deepseek-harness-desktop)'s convenience layer, so the same features run inside dsh itself: no desktop shell, no Tauri, no extra process.

## Plugins

| Package | What it does | Command |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |
| `dsh-features` | The hub (Features): one sidebar entry between Plugins and Scheduled tasks, lists every installed feature plugin as a row like dsh's own Plugins page, opens one on click, reorders by drag. Install it to lose the floating corner buttons | |
| `dsh-skills` | Manage skills: enable / disable / delete / import, including local ZIP archives | `/skills` |
| `dsh-mcp` | Manage MCP servers in the active profile's patch layer: add / edit / delete / enable / import | `/mcp` |
| `dsh-doctor` | Harness diagnostics: version, port, pid, profile, log tail | `/doctor` |
| `dsh-zoom` | Page zoom with rebindable shortcuts | `/zoom` |
| `dsh-notify` | Task reminders: in-page popup, bundled sounds, browser notification | `/notify` |
| `dsh-remote` | Phone remote access: authenticated reverse proxy, QR link, optional Cloudflare tunnel, mobile UI rewrite, project browser | `/remote` |
| `dsh-init` | Write or update this workspace's `AGENTS.md`, the instruction file dsh loads into every session there | `/init` |

Each one is a normal dsh plugin: it declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` mounts its layer automatically. They never import each other, so any subset works.

`dsh-init` is a command, not a feature: no browser half, no panel, no `dsh.ui.feature` marker, so
`dsh-features` does not list it. That matches the built-in `/init` it was ported from. Its prompt is
written against the harness's real instruction-loading chain (the root `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`,
the personal overlays, nested files, and the user-global file it must not touch), and it arrives as a
collapsed context row rather than a long user message.

`dsh-features` is not a feature but the hub the other packages plug into. It is the only one with a
browser half (`dsh.client` → `lib/client.js`), because a real navigation entry can only be added by
a dsh client plugin. With it installed, feature panels move onto the hub's page and their floating
corner buttons disappear; uninstall it and the buttons come back, unchanged.

## Install

Each package installs on its own, and both routes take the same specs: the desktop app's **Plugins**
page, or `dsh plugin add` from a command line. Restart dsh afterwards; plugins have no HMR.

### One by one in the desktop app

The official desktop app manages its own `desktop` profile, and the command line cannot change that
one. Open **Plugins**, then **Add plugin**, paste one spec, install, and repeat for the next. The
box accepts a package name, a Git repository address, or a local directory path.

```text
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-features
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-skills
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-mcp
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-doctor
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-zoom
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-notify
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-remote
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-init
```

`#path:/<package>` is pnpm's subdirectory-of-a-repository form; all eight live in this one
repository, so every spec carries it. Order does not matter, and a subset is fine. Install
`dsh-features` too and the feature panels move onto its single sidebar entry instead of one
floating corner button each. A pinned spec needs no escaping here; the `&` trap belongs to the
command line, not to the page.

The page itself tells you two things. Upgrading is uninstall, then install the new version: there
is no auto-update, so a fix arrives by reinstalling the spec, pinned if you want it reproducible.
And when GitHub cannot be reached, retry with the page's **Install source** choice: default, npm
official, China mirror, or custom.

### From the command line

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-skills
# pin a commit:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#<sha>&path:/dsh-skills
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-skills
```

`--profile web` is DSHDesktop's shell profile; the desktop app's profile goes through its page, above.

**Pinning a commit on Windows.** `dsh plugin` runs through the app's `dsh.cmd` shim, and cmd.exe
eats the `&` in `#<sha>&path:/dsh…`, so pnpm receives a bare `#<sha>` and refuses it. Pin from
the app's page, where the spec goes straight to pnpm, or install the branch spec instead.

**If pnpm cannot reach github.com.** It fetches with its own TLS stack and ignores the system
proxy, so a TLS-intercepting network fails with `TypeError: fetch failed`. Write
`https-proxy=http://127.0.0.1:7890` and `proxy=http://127.0.0.1:7890` into
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/.npmrc`, or install offline: copy a package into
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/plugins/<name>/` and add that directory path.

## Conventions

- **Independent by construction.** No package imports another; each duplicates the small layout and HTTP helpers it needs, so a missing, drifted or uninstalled sibling breaks nothing.
- **One DOM-level agreement.** Launchers dock into a shared `#dsh-launchers` corner container, and panels clear it via the published `--dsh-launcher-stack` height.
- **The hub agreement.** A feature publishes `{ title, order, mount(host) }` to `window.__dshFeatures` and declares `dsh.ui.feature` in its package.json; the hub mounts it inline and hides `#dsh-launchers`. Nothing is imported in either direction.
- **Bilingual panels, theme-following colours.** Language comes from `navigator.language`, deliberately not dsh's `locale`, which would make every package parse the profile patch. Colours prefer the shell's own `--dsw-alias-*` tokens, so a panel follows dsh's light/dark setting, and fall back to hardcoded values under `prefers-color-scheme`.
- **Compared to the retired single-package `dsh-desktop-kit`:** no page-error reporting. That package was the origin these were split from and is no longer developed.

Development notes and the traps worth knowing live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Test

```bash
cd <name> && node tests/<name>.test.mjs
node tests/hub-contract.test.mjs          # repo-wide: the hub agreement, from the root
node tests/panel-embed.test.mjs           # repo-wide: every panel boots without the hub
node tests/mobile-layer.test.mjs          # repo-wide: the phone layer's DOM behaviour
node tests/manifest.test.mjs              # repo-wide: the directory name, and every import declared
```

Offline suites: 88 (dsh-features) / 60 / 20 / 23 / 23 / 38 / 99 checks, plus 49 (dsh-init) and 279
repo-wide contract checks, 78 cross-package panel checks, 7 mobile-layer checks and 17 manifest
checks.

`dsh-features`' suite evaluates its browser half for real (a vm with a minimal React), so the
sidebar slot, its order, the list, the drill-down and the mount hand-off are asserted without a
browser. `dsh-init`'s suite runs the runtime's own session-format V4 admission on the message it
injects, with a negative fixture proving the probe can fail, so the one regression that makes `/init`
register and then do nothing stays caught. `panel-embed.test.mjs` runs all six feature panels'
scripts in a DOM stub to prove none of them docks a corner button or a second refresh control while
the hub is installed. `mobile-layer.test.mjs` does the same for the browser half of the phone layer,
where a remote-origin settings page has to lose upstream's dead Retry.
`tools/visual/` holds a screenshot harness for the UI work these numbers cannot see; see its README.
`dsh-remote` also ships a live suite (`tests/remote-live.mjs`) that needs a sandbox instance with
remote access enabled.

## License

MIT. Sounds under `dsh-notify/lib/sounds/` come from opencode via DSHDesktop; the mobile assets under `dsh-remote/lib/assets/` are vendored from DSHDesktop.

# dsh-features

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

One home for this repository's feature plugins: a single sidebar entry, **Features**, between Plugins
and Scheduled tasks, whose page mounts every installed feature plugin inline under one skin — instead
of a stack of floating corner buttons over dsh's own UI.

This package is not a feature itself. It is the hub the other `dsh-*` packages plug into, and it is
built as a **client plugin**: the page, the sidebar glyph and the stylesheet are a browser bundle
(`lib/client.js`) that dsh's own client module system serves, which is the only way to add a real
navigation entry. It needs no other plugin, and the other packages need no change to work without it.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-features
# pin a commit:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#<sha>&path:/dsh-features
```

`--profile web` = DSHDesktop's shell, `--profile desktop` = the official desktop app; the panel needs
no flag. Restart dsh afterwards — plugins have no HMR.

## What it does

- **A real nav entry.** `sidebar.panellist` at `order: 5`; the official entries are Plugins (`0`) and
  Scheduled tasks (`10`), and the sidebar sorts that slot by `order`.
- **A page that hosts the features.** A list of rows, one per installed feature plugin, laid out like
  dsh's own Plugins page: glyph, name, summary, chevron. **Clicking a row opens that feature's settings**
  on the same page, with a back control in the head. Rows are **draggable into your own order**, kept
  in `localStorage` (`dsh-features:nav-order`) — the same per-origin storage dsh itself uses for UI
  preferences. **One refresh control exists at a time**, in the page head: it rescans the inventory
  and remounts the open feature, so embedded panels hide their own (and the hub sweeps away a
  leftover one from an older panel build). Below 620px the gutters tighten for the phone remote view.
  Features stay standalone — the hub calls into them.
- **One skin.** The stylesheet hides `#dsh-launchers` (no more stacked buttons) and publishes the
  same `--dsh-*` token palette the feature panels already use, so a feature looks the same inline as
  it does in its own floating panel. Every colour prefers the shell's own theme token
  (`--dsw-alias-*`, which follows dsh's light/dark setting) and falls back to a hardcoded value, so
  the hub matches dsh's theme instead of guessing from the OS.
- **Named failures.** A feature the profile declares but whose browser half never loaded is listed as
  *installed, but its panel did not load* rather than silently missing. Declared is the operative word:
  a package merely staged in `<DSH_HOME>/profiles/plugins/<name>/` is not installed, and does not
  appear — that directory is where a manual install is prepared, not evidence of one.

## Routes

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| ------ | ---- | ------- |
| GET | `/dsh-features/api/status` | `{ ok, hub, route, version }` — the probe feature panels use |
| GET | `/dsh-features/api/features` | the inventory: packages *this profile declares* (its `dependencies` / `dsh.profile.bundles`) that declare `dsh.ui.feature`, plus `navOrder` |
| POST | `/dsh-features/api/order` | save the reader's feature order: `{ keys: [...] }`, answered with the stored order |

Read-only except the order, credential-free, and same-origin with the page.

## The two contracts

Everything else is independent — no shared module, no sibling import. Two conventions are the whole
interface, both DOM-level:

**1. A feature publishes itself to the hub** (this is what makes a feature appear, and how the hub
mounts it):

```js
window.__dshFeatures = Object.assign(window.__dshFeatures ?? {}, {
  doctor: {
    title: "Doctor",                    // nav label (already localized by the feature)
    icon: "M2 8.5h3l1.5-4 2.5 7 ...",   // optional 16×16 stroke SVG path for the nav row
    order: 30,                          // default nav order (the reader's drag order wins)
    mount(host) { /* render into host */ }   // called on every visit; must be re-mountable
  }
});
```

**2. A feature declares the same thing for the inventory** (metadata only — it lets the hub name a
feature whose script failed):

```json
"dsh": { "ui": { "feature": {
  "key": "doctor", "order": 30,
  "title": { "zh": "<Chinese label>", "en": "Doctor" },
  "summary": { "zh": "<Chinese summary>", "en": "Status and log tail" }
} } }
```

A feature also probes `GET /dsh-features/api/status` at boot: when the hub answers, the feature does
**not** dock its own corner button, because its UI is reachable from the hub page. When the route is
absent (no hub installed — a bare dsh, or a profile without this package), the floating panel is
built exactly as before. Uninstalling this package therefore restores the buttons.

## Data

`<DSH_HOME>/dsh-features.json` — the reader's feature order, written atomically through
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write`. It is on the host rather than in the browser because browser storage is
per-origin and the phone reaches the same dsh from the proxy's origin: kept in `localStorage` (where it
used to live) a desktop reorder never reached the phone. The page still caches it locally, which is what
gives the first frame the right order; the host's answer is what it reconciles against.

## Caveats

- The page mounts a feature into its own DOM on open and drops it on the way back, so a feature's UI
  is rebuilt on every visit. A feature whose background work updates its panel only repaints while
  it is open.
- Feature panels are third-party code running in the page. The hub hands them a node and calls
  `mount`; it does not sandbox them (dsh's own client plugins share the page the same way).
- The hub removes any bare refresh button a mounted feature renders (the `Refresh` literal, or its
  localized form), and anything marked `data-dsh-refresh`: the page head owns the only refresh control. A feature with a control of its
  own that must survive should label it something else.
- The sidebar position is a number (`order: 5`). If a future dsh release adds an entry between 0 and
  10, that entry and this one swap places.
- `#dsh-launchers` is hidden globally while this package is installed. That is the point of the
  package; uninstall it to get the floating buttons back.

## Test

```bash
cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/plugins/dsh-features"
node tests/hub.test.mjs
```

The browser half is evaluated for real in that suite (a vm with a minimal React), so the sidebar
slot, the order, the skin, the list, the drill-down, the drag order and the mount hand-off are all
asserted without a browser. The repository root has one more suite that runs every feature panel's
browser script against the hub's behaviour: `node tests/panel-embed.test.mjs`.

## License

MIT.

The `/init` command: write or update this workspace's `AGENTS.md`, the instruction file dsh injects
into every future session in that workspace.

was: it spells out how this harness actually loads instruction files, so the generated file follows
the real rules instead of generic advice.

## What it does

`/init [extra instructions]` submits one prompt to the agent and returns immediately. The agent then
reads the workspace, and creates or incrementally updates `AGENTS.md` at the workspace root, guided
by:

- the whole loading chain this harness uses: `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at the root, the
  `*.local.md` personal overlays, nested files that outrank the root one for work under their
  directory, and the user-global `~/.dsh/AGENTS.md` it must **not** touch;
- what to write: purpose and layout, the real build/test/lint commands, architecture boundaries,
  conventions, and the gotchas a newcomer trips over;
- what not to write: anything obvious from a quick look at the repo, and anything long, since the
  file enters the context of every session.

Text typed after the command rides along as extra instructions, which is how you steer it ("keep it
under 40 lines", "the build command needs `--frozen-lockfile`").

The prompt arrives as a **collapsed context row** in the transcript, not as a long user message. A
command may only return one line of text, so the prompt is queued on the agent's next turn with a
producer-owned message source; that is also what keeps `/init` readable rather than a wall of orange.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-init
```

`--profile web` = DSHDesktop's shell, `--profile desktop` = the official desktop app.

## Name ownership

`init` is a first-come, first-served command name, and one other plugin claims it:

- **DSHDesktop's built-in `dsh-command-init`**, preseeded into the shell's own profile. If both are
  installed, dsh registers whichever loads first, warns, and deactivates the other. Pick one.

during `apply` would take the whole plugin tree down.

None. It is a command, not a feature: there is nothing to display, so it declares no

the built-in it was ported from.


own V4 admission **accepts** the submitted message, with a negative fixture proving the probe can
fail. That is the regression worth guarding: a retired message source registers fine, does nothing,

# dsh-mcp

Manage MCP servers from inside [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness):
add, edit, delete, enable/disable, and import from other agent tool configs.

Ported from DSHDesktop's MCP page. It edits the active profile's `cordis.patch.yml` through the
`yaml` document API — the same approach as dsh's own `dsh-config-editor` — so **your comments and
`!!js` expression tags survive**, and editing an existing server keeps the advanced keys the form
does not own (`toolCallTimeoutMs`, `reconnect`, …). Writes go through `writeFileAtomic` with the
package's file lock, serialized against the loader's hot reload.

## Placement

With **[dsh-features](../dsh-features)** (the Features hub) installed, this panel appears on that hub's single
page and no longer docks its own corner button; without the hub — a bare dsh, or a profile where it is
not installed — the floating panel is built exactly as before. The coupling is two DOM-level
conventions (`window.__dshFeatures`, `#dsh-launchers`), described in the repository's AGENTS.md.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-mcp
# pin a commit:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#<sha>&path:/dsh-mcp
```

`--profile web` = DSHDesktop's shell, `--profile desktop` = the official desktop app; the panel needs no flag.

Restart dsh afterwards — plugins have no HMR. Server edits themselves do *not* need a restart: dsh
hot-reloads the patch layer.

## What it does

- **List** the MCP servers in the active profile's patch layer, with transport, a one-line summary
  and enabled state.
- **Add / edit** a server: `stdio` (command, arguments, env, cwd) or `streamable-http` (url, headers).
- **Enable / disable** by setting `disabled: true` on the row.
- **Delete** a server row.
- **Import** from other agent tool configs found under `$HOME` (Claude-style `.mcp.json`,
  Codex-style TOML, …); servers whose transport this plugin cannot express are shown greyed out.
- **`/mcp`** prints the same list as text, without the browser.

## Routes

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| ------ | ---- | ------- |
| GET | `/dsh-mcp/panel.js` `/dsh-mcp/panel.css` | browser half |
| GET | `/dsh-mcp/api/mcp` | servers + importable sources + counts + patch path |
| POST | `/dsh-mcp/api/mcp` | `upsert` · `toggle` · `delete` · `import` |

## Data

| What | Where |
| ---- | ----- |
| MCP servers | `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, as `insert` rows |

This package keeps no settings file of its own.

## Test

```bash
# from an installed copy (needs `yaml` and @deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write via the profile)
cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/plugins/dsh-mcp"
node tests/mcp.test.mjs
```

The test guards the thing that matters: a round trip through the editor must leave every other row,
every comment and every `!!js` tag intact.

## License

MIT.

# dsh-plugin

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Small independent [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) plugins: one feature per package, each installable on its own. | `dsh-mcp` | Manage MCP servers in the active profile's patch layer: add / edit / delete / enable / import | `/mcp` |
| `dsh-doctor` | Harness diagnostics: version, port, pid, profile, log tail | `/doctor` |
| `dsh-zoom` | Page zoom with rebindable shortcuts | `/zoom` |
| `dsh-notify` | Task reminders: in-page popup, bundled sounds, browser notification | `/notify` |
| `dsh-remote` | Phone remote access: authenticated reverse proxy, QR link, optional Cloudflare tunnel, mobile UI rewrite, project browser | `/remote` |
| `dsh-init` | Write or update this workspace's `AGENTS.md`, the instruction file dsh loads into every session there | `/init` |

`dsh-features` does not list it. That matches the built-in `/init` it was ported from. Its prompt is
written against the harness's real instruction-loading chain (the root `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`,
the personal overlays, nested files, and the user-global file it must not touch), and it arrives as a
collapsed context row rather than a long user message.

`dsh-features` is not a feature but the hub the other packages plug into. It is the only one with a
browser half (`dsh.client` → `lib/client.js`), because a real navigation entry can only be added by
a dsh client plugin. With it installed, feature panels move onto the hub's page and their floating
corner buttons disappear; uninstall it and the buttons come back, unchanged.

page, or `dsh plugin add` from a command line. Restart dsh afterwards; plugins have no HMR.

one. Open **Plugins**, then **Add plugin**, paste one spec, install, and repeat for the next. The
box accepts a package name, a Git repository address, or a local directory path.

```text
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-features
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-skills
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-mcp
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-doctor
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-zoom
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-notify
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-remote
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-init
```

`#path:/<package>` is pnpm's subdirectory-of-a-repository form; all eight live in this one
repository, so every spec carries it. Order does not matter, and a subset is fine. Install
`dsh-features` too and the feature panels move onto its single sidebar entry instead of one
floating corner button each. A pinned spec needs no escaping here; the `&` trap belongs to the
command line, not to the page.

The page itself tells you two things. Upgrading is uninstall, then install the new version: there
is no auto-update, so a fix arrives by reinstalling the spec, pinned if you want it reproducible.

official, China mirror, or custom.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-skills
# pin a commit:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#<sha>&path:/dsh-skills
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-skills
```

# dsh-notify

Task reminders inside dsh: a popup, a sound and a browser notification, for four kinds of events.

Ported from DSHDesktop, which raised Windows toasts from WinRT and played WAV files on a
self-managed `waveOut` thread. Neither exists inside dsh, so the split is: the host half subscribes
to dsh's own events and republishes them on a small SSE stream, and the browser half plays the sound
and shows the notification.

Why subscribe host-side instead of having the page connect to `/api/remote.mux`: the page would have
to replay the frame protocol (stream ids, `$events` waterflow acks, per-session `session/follow`)
that the desktop shell implements in Rust. `ctx.on(...)` host-side is far less code and far less
likely to break on a dsh upgrade — and SSE reconnects on its own.

## Placement

With **[dsh-features](../dsh-features)** (the Features hub) installed, this panel appears on that hub's single
page and no longer docks its own corner button; without the hub — a bare dsh, or a profile where it is
not installed — the floating panel is built exactly as before. The coupling is two DOM-level
conventions (`window.__dshFeatures`, `#dsh-launchers`), described in the repository's AGENTS.md.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-notify
# pin a commit:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#<sha>&path:/dsh-notify
```

`--profile web` = DSHDesktop's shell, `--profile desktop` = the official desktop app; the panel needs no flag.

Restart dsh afterwards — plugins have no HMR.

## The four kinds

| Kind | Raised when |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `approval` | an operation is waiting for your approval |
| `question` | a question is waiting for your answer |
| `turn_done` | a turn finished and it had used at least one tool |
| `answer_done` | a turn finished and it was a plain answer |

Subagent turns are suppressed, and a turn that did not end with `reason.kind == "completed"` is not
reported — the same rules the desktop shell applies.

Each kind has an **on/off** switch and a **timing**: *always*, or *only when this page is not focused*
(the default — no point popping a toast you are already looking at).

Channels: an in-page popup, a sound (a bundled 17-sound pack, the system default, or silent), and a
browser notification (needs permission once). Volume 0–1.

## Routes

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| ------ | ---- | ------- |
| GET | `/dsh-notify/panel.js` `/dsh-notify/panel.css` | browser half |
| GET | `/dsh-notify/api/settings` | settings + the bundled sound list |
| POST | `/dsh-notify/api/settings` | deep-merged settings patch |
| GET | `/dsh-notify/api/events` | SSE reminder stream |
| GET | `/dsh-notify/api/notifications` | the last 50 reminders |
| GET | `/dsh-notify/sounds/<id>.wav` | the bundled sound pack |

## Data

| What | Where |
| ---- | ----- |
| The four rules, sound, volume, popup and browser toggles | `$DSH_HOME/dsh-notify.json` |

## Caveats

- The **sound is played by the browser** (`HTMLAudioElement`), not by a native audio thread, so the
  browser's autoplay policy can block it until you have interacted with the page. The popup and the
  system notification are unaffected.
- **Browser notifications need permission** (and a secure context — `127.0.0.1` counts as one).
- The panel must be open in some tab for reminders to be raised at all: the SSE stream lives in the
  page. Reminders are per-browser, not per-machine.

## Test

```bash
cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/plugins/dsh-notify"
node tests/notify.test.mjs
```

## License

MIT. The WAV files under `lib/sounds/` come from opencode via DSHDesktop and are copied as-is.

# dsh-remote

Reach your DeepSeek Harness from your phone.

dsh binds the loopback address only, and its session cookie is bound to the authority it was issued
for — so a remote authority (a LAN address, a tunnel hostname) can never present a valid cookie. This
plugin runs a small **authenticated reverse proxy inside the dsh process**: the phone talks to the
proxy, and the proxy re-issues the request to dsh's loopback address with a cookie it holds
(exchanged from `ctx.connection`'s launch token). Ported from DSHDesktop's remote page.

## Placement

With **[dsh-features](../dsh-features)** (the Features hub) installed, this panel appears on that hub's single
page and no longer docks its own corner button; without the hub — a bare dsh, or a profile where it is
not installed — the floating panel is built exactly as before. The coupling is two DOM-level
conventions (`window.__dshFeatures`, `#dsh-launchers`), described in the repository's AGENTS.md.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-remote
# pin a commit:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#<sha>&path:/dsh-remote
```

`--profile web` = DSHDesktop's shell, `--profile desktop` = the official desktop app; the panel needs no flag.

Restart dsh afterwards — plugins have no HMR.

## Channels

| Channel | Reaches | Notes |
| ------- | ------- | ----- |
| LAN | nothing leaves your network | binds `0.0.0.0`; open `http://<lan-ip>:<port>/?token=…` on the phone; no extra binary |
| Tunnel | the public internet | also spawns `cloudflared` (Cloudflare quick tunnel); see the caveat below about finding it |

**Off by default** — the link is the only credential, and enabling publishes your harness to whoever
holds it.

## Response-side work

Not a plain passthrough; four needle-anchored rewrites a drifted dsh frontend simply skips:

- **Mobile UI** — document navigations get `mobile.css`/`mobile.js` (narrow-screen layout, iOS
  keyboard/viewport fixes), a splash overlay, and a no-zoom viewport meta. Assets are never rewritten.
- **Project browser** — `/dsh-remote/project`: read-only file tree, mapped to the current session's
  workspace via dsh's `storages/workspace.json`; previews (8 MB) and downloads (64 MB, RFC 5987
  filenames), paths confined to the workspace.
- **gzip** — text assets ≥4 KB, on request (saves the Cloudflare leg).
- **Idle keepalives** — against Cloudflare's ~100 s idle kill: the WS bridge Pings after 30 s of
  downstream silence, but only with no partial frame buffered; a quiet `text/event-stream` gets a
  `: keepalive` line. A busy channel gets nothing.

If the bundled assets are missing the proxy degrades to passthrough rather than failing requests.

## Routes

Served by dsh's origin, behind its gate:

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| ------ | ---- | ------- |
| GET | `/dsh-remote/panel.js` `/dsh-remote/panel.css` | browser half |
| GET | `/dsh-remote/api/remote` | state, link, LAN addresses, cloudflared path |
| POST | `/dsh-remote/api/remote` | `enable` · `disable` · `mode` · `reset-token` |
| GET | `/dsh-remote/api/status` | the same state **without** the credential |
| GET | `/dsh-remote/qr.svg` | QR code for the current link |

The project browser is served by the **proxy**, so it needs the link's token:
`/dsh-remote/project` and `/dsh-remote/project/api/*`.

## The gate

256-bit token compared in constant time; `?token=…` is exchanged for an `HttpOnly` cookie via a 303
(the token never stays in an address bar); a wrong token waits 500 ms before its 403; the token is
never logged. Disabling revokes the cookie, and *Reset link* invalidates every link shared before it.

## Data

| What | Where |
| ---- | ----- |
| Enabled, channel, port, token, cloudflared path | `$DSH_HOME/dsh-remote.json` |

Token and port persist, so **a saved LAN link survives a dsh restart** (a tunnel URL cannot —
Cloudflare assigns a new hostname each time).

## The phone's page

The proxy rewrites dsh's HTML: it injects `assets/mobile.css` + `assets/mobile.js` before `</head>`, which
is where the phone-only fixes live — the project browser tab, the attachment button, the viewport reset,
and three compensations for upstream behaviour that will not change:

- **The preview notice is re-shown on every remote load.** Upstream stores its acknowledgement in a
  settings scope whose persistence follows the transport, and for a remote browser that scope is
  memory-mode ("the acknowledgement stays process-local here"), so it never persists. `mobile.js` clicks
  its Continue control as soon as the modal appears and marks its portal, which `mobile.css` hides — the
  click matters as much as the hide, because the modal holds `#root` inert while it is up.
- **The settings sheet cannot work as designed at 390 px.** Its panel is 800 px wide with a fixed 188 px nav
  column beside the content, which on a phone leaves the content a sliver; the sheet is made a full-screen
  flex column whose nav becomes a centred tab strip with a safe-area inset at the top. Measured on the real
  page, four tabs are 401 px of content in a 390 px screen, so the strip centres them and wraps rather than
  scrolling — a scrollbar at that size just means the last tab is invisible and nobody discovers it.
- **The models tab cannot read settings from a remote page at all.** Upstream loads the provider directory
  from a settings "describe face", and a remote transport has no view for it, so the page fails with
  `加载提供商目录失败: settings are unavailable in this browser` and Retry never helps. That boundary is
  deliberate — it is what stops a link-holder from rewriting the host's settings and API keys — so the layer
  does not fake a loopback origin. It only adds a line under the failure saying where to change it.

All three match on the exact upstream wording and on `[class*="_…"]` local-name substrings, so an upstream
rename degrades to "the phone looks like it did before" rather than breaking the page.

## The link survives a restart

The link is the credential, so a restart must not invalidate it. A Cloudflare *quick* tunnel gets a fresh
random hostname every time cloudflared starts, which would mean re-scanning the QR code after every restart —
so, like the desktop shell, this plugin keeps the tunnel instead:

- cloudflared is spawned **detached**, with its output going to `<DSH_HOME>/dsh-remote-tunnel.log` rather
  than to the plugin's pipes. A pipe would break the moment dsh exits, and cloudflared dying on a write
  error is exactly the churn this avoids.
- Its hostname, pid and target are recorded in `<DSH_HOME>/dsh-remote-session.json`.
- The next start **adopts** that tunnel instead of spawning one, provided the record agrees with this run
  (same binary, same proxy target) **and** the tunnel still answers for the current token — one probe
  covers both a dead process and a tunnel pointing at a proxy port that no longer exists. The panel then
  says the link is unchanged.
- The proxy rebinds the remembered port for the same reason, so the tunnel's target stays valid.
- Disabling remote access is the one path that kills the tunnel and forgets the session (the next enable
  then mints a new link, which is what "disable" has to mean). On unload the plugin only stops supervising.

If any check fails, the plugin kills the stale tunnel and starts a fresh one — a new hostname, the same
token, so the old link stops working and the panel shows the new one.

## Caveats

- **Tunnel mode needs a cloudflared binary, and neither app ships one.** The search is, in order: the
  `cloudflaredPath` setting, the directory holding the running runtime (`process.execPath`, which is
  where the shell keeps its own copy), `<dsh home>/../tunnel/`, every `PATH` entry, then the winget shim
  and the MSI install directory. On a machine with none of those the panel says where it looked and
  takes a path (saved to `$DSH_HOME/dsh-remote.json`); `winget install Cloudflare.cloudflared` is the
  one-line fix. LAN mode needs no binary at all.
- **The tunnel does not survive dsh.** The desktop shell keeps cloudflared outside its Job Object; a
  plugin inside the process cannot, so the tunnel URL changes every restart. Reconnects back off
  500 ms → 30 s, then retry forever.
- **A quick tunnel is a single connection.** If your ISP reclaims idle QUIC/UDP sessions the link
  dies, which is why the tunnel is spawned pinned to `--protocol http2`.
- **The QR code needs `qrcode`.** A git/npm install brings it along, verified. A *local path* install
  makes a `link:` dependency and pnpm skips a linked package's own dependencies — run `npm install`
  inside the plugin directory in that case, or the panel shows the install hint instead of the symbol
  (the link still works).

## Test

```bash
cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/plugins/dsh-remote"
node tests/proxy.test.mjs     # frame bridge, HTML/gzip/SSE rewrites, project routes
```

`tests/remote-live.mjs <baseUrl> <proxyPort> <token>` is a live suite; it opens and closes remote
access on the instance it targets, so point it at a sandbox — never at a harness someone is using.

## License

MIT. The mobile assets under `lib/assets/` are vendored from DSHDesktop (also MIT).

# dsh-plugin

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Small independent [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) plugins: one feature per package, each installable on its own. Ported out of [DSHDesktop](https://github.com/LBurny/deepseek-harness-desktop)'s convenience layer, so the same features run inside dsh itself: no desktop shell, no Tauri, no extra process.

## Plugins

| Package | What it does | Command |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |
| `dsh-features` | The hub (Features): one sidebar entry between Plugins and Scheduled tasks, lists every installed feature plugin as a row like dsh's own Plugins page, opens one on click, reorders by drag. Install it to lose the floating corner buttons | |
| `dsh-skills` | Manage skills: enable / disable / delete / import, including local ZIP archives | `/skills` |
| `dsh-mcp` | Manage MCP servers in the active profile's patch layer: add / edit / delete / enable / import | `/mcp` |
| `dsh-doctor` | Harness diagnostics: version, port, pid, profile, log tail | `/doctor` |
| `dsh-zoom` | Page zoom with rebindable shortcuts | `/zoom` |
| `dsh-notify` | Task reminders: in-page popup, bundled sounds, browser notification | `/notify` |
| `dsh-remote` | Phone remote access: authenticated reverse proxy, QR link, optional Cloudflare tunnel, mobile UI rewrite, project browser | `/remote` |
| `dsh-init` | Write or update this workspace's `AGENTS.md`, the instruction file dsh loads into every session there | `/init` |

Each one is a normal dsh plugin: it declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` mounts its layer automatically. They never import each other, so any subset works.

`dsh-init` is a command, not a feature: no browser half, no panel, no `dsh.ui.feature` marker, so
`dsh-features` does not list it. That matches the built-in `/init` it was ported from. Its prompt is
written against the harness's real instruction-loading chain (the root `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`,
the personal overlays, nested files, and the user-global file it must not touch), and it arrives as a
collapsed context row rather than a long user message.

`dsh-features` is not a feature but the hub the other packages plug into. It is the only one with a
browser half (`dsh.client` → `lib/client.js`), because a real navigation entry can only be added by
a dsh client plugin. With it installed, feature panels move onto the hub's page and their floating
corner buttons disappear; uninstall it and the buttons come back, unchanged.

## Install

Each package installs on its own, and both routes take the same specs: the desktop app's **Plugins**
page, or `dsh plugin add` from a command line. Restart dsh afterwards; plugins have no HMR.

### One by one in the desktop app

The official desktop app manages its own `desktop` profile, and the command line cannot change that
one. Open **Plugins**, then **Add plugin**, paste one spec, install, and repeat for the next. The
box accepts a package name, a Git repository address, or a local directory path.

```text
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-features
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-skills
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-mcp
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-doctor
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-zoom
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-notify
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-remote
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-init
```

`#path:/<package>` is pnpm's subdirectory-of-a-repository form; all eight live in this one
repository, so every spec carries it. Order does not matter, and a subset is fine. Install
`dsh-features` too and the feature panels move onto its single sidebar entry instead of one
floating corner button each. A pinned spec needs no escaping here; the `&` trap belongs to the
command line, not to the page.

The page itself tells you two things. Upgrading is uninstall, then install the new version: there
is no auto-update, so a fix arrives by reinstalling the spec, pinned if you want it reproducible.
And when GitHub cannot be reached, retry with the page's **Install source** choice: default, npm
official, China mirror, or custom.

### From the command line

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-skills
# pin a commit:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#<sha>&path:/dsh-skills
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-skills
```

`--profile web` is DSHDesktop's shell profile; the desktop app's profile goes through its page, above.

**Pinning a commit on Windows.** `dsh plugin` runs through the app's `dsh.cmd` shim, and cmd.exe
eats the `&` in `#<sha>&path:/dsh…`, so pnpm receives a bare `#<sha>` and refuses it. Pin from
the app's page, where the spec goes straight to pnpm, or install the branch spec instead.

**If pnpm cannot reach github.com.** It fetches with its own TLS stack and ignores the system
proxy, so a TLS-intercepting network fails with `TypeError: fetch failed`. Write
`https-proxy=http://127.0.0.1:7890` and `proxy=http://127.0.0.1:7890` into
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/.npmrc`, or install offline: copy a package into
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/plugins/<name>/` and add that directory path.

## Conventions

- **Independent by construction.** No package imports another; each duplicates the small layout and HTTP helpers it needs, so a missing, drifted or uninstalled sibling breaks nothing.
- **One DOM-level agreement.** Launchers dock into a shared `#dsh-launchers` corner container, and panels clear it via the published `--dsh-launcher-stack` height.
- **The hub agreement.** A feature publishes `{ title, order, mount(host) }` to `window.__dshFeatures` and declares `dsh.ui.feature` in its package.json; the hub mounts it inline and hides `#dsh-launchers`. Nothing is imported in either direction.
- **Bilingual panels, theme-following colours.** Language comes from `navigator.language`, deliberately not dsh's `locale`, which would make every package parse the profile patch. Colours prefer the shell's own `--dsw-alias-*` tokens, so a panel follows dsh's light/dark setting, and fall back to hardcoded values under `prefers-color-scheme`.
- **Compared to the retired single-package `dsh-desktop-kit`:** no page-error reporting. That package was the origin these were split from and is no longer developed.

Development notes and the traps worth knowing live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Test

```bash
cd <name> && node tests/<name>.test.mjs
node tests/hub-contract.test.mjs          # repo-wide: the hub agreement, from the root
node tests/panel-embed.test.mjs           # repo-wide: every panel boots without the hub
node tests/mobile-layer.test.mjs          # repo-wide: the phone layer's DOM behaviour
node tests/manifest.test.mjs              # repo-wide: the directory name, and every import declared
```

Offline suites: 88 (dsh-features) / 60 / 20 / 23 / 23 / 38 / 99 checks, plus 49 (dsh-init) and 279
repo-wide contract checks, 78 cross-package panel checks, 7 mobile-layer checks and 17 manifest
checks.

`dsh-features`' suite evaluates its browser half for real (a vm with a minimal React), so the
sidebar slot, its order, the list, the drill-down and the mount hand-off are asserted without a
browser. `dsh-init`'s suite runs the runtime's own session-format V4 admission on the message it
injects, with a negative fixture proving the probe can fail, so the one regression that makes `/init`
register and then do nothing stays caught. `panel-embed.test.mjs` runs all six feature panels'
scripts in a DOM stub to prove none of them docks a corner button or a second refresh control while
the hub is installed. `mobile-layer.test.mjs` does the same for the browser half of the phone layer,
where a remote-origin settings page has to lose upstream's dead Retry.
`tools/visual/` holds a screenshot harness for the UI work these numbers cannot see; see its README.
`dsh-remote` also ships a live suite (`tests/remote-live.mjs`) that needs a sandbox instance with
remote access enabled.

## License

MIT. Sounds under `dsh-notify/lib/sounds/` come from opencode via DSHDesktop; the mobile assets under `dsh-remote/lib/assets/` are vendored from DSHDesktop.

# dsh-skills

Manage [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) skills from inside dsh:
list, enable/disable, delete, and import — including from a local ZIP archive.

Ported from DSHDesktop's skills page. The desktop shell moved skill directories around from a Tauri
command; this does the same inside the dsh process, so dsh's own file watcher picks the change up
without a restart.

## Placement

With **[dsh-features](../dsh-features)** (the Features hub) installed, this panel appears on that hub's single
page and no longer docks its own corner button; without the hub — a bare dsh, or a profile where it is
not installed — the floating panel is built exactly as before. The coupling is two DOM-level
conventions (`window.__dshFeatures`, `#dsh-launchers`), described in the repository's AGENTS.md.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-skills
# pin a commit:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#<sha>&path:/dsh-skills
```

`--profile web` = DSHDesktop's shell, `--profile desktop` = the official desktop app; the panel needs no flag.

Restart dsh afterwards — plugins have no HMR.

## What it does

- **List** the skills dsh can see, with their enabled state and description.
- **Enable / disable** by moving the skill directory between `$DSH_HOME/skills/` (scanned by dsh's
  filesystem provider) and `$DSH_HOME/skills-disabled/` (not scanned). A directory counts as a skill
  when it contains `SKILL.md`.
- **Delete** a skill from either root.
- **Import** from other agent tool roots (Claude / Codex style skill directories, greying out the
  ones that are absent), or from a **local ZIP archive**. Source directories are commonly symlink
  farms (one shared checkout linked into every tool), so a symlinked entry counts as a skill and is
  copied as real files rather than re-linked. The ZIP reader only reads the central directory,
  supports stored and deflate entries, and enforces entry/size caps plus traversal rejection; a pack
  may hold one skill (`SKILL.md` at the archive root) or many (`<dir>/SKILL.md`).
- **`/skills`** prints the same list as text, without the browser.

A skill's toggle takes effect through dsh's watcher, so no restart is needed. The panel appears in
the corner of the dsh web UI, next to any other dsh-plugin packages you have installed.

## Routes

Everything hangs off `/dsh-skills` and is protected by dsh's own origin gate.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| ------ | ---- | ------- |
| GET | `/dsh-skills/panel.js` `/dsh-skills/panel.css` | browser half |
| GET | `/dsh-skills/api/skills` | skills + importable sources + counts |
| POST | `/dsh-skills/api/skills` | `toggle` · `delete` · `import` · `import-zip` |
| POST | `/dsh-skills/api/skills/zip` | ZIP import step 1: upload (≤64 MiB), get discovered skills + an upload id |

The upload is held in memory between the two steps (10 min TTL, at most 4 at a time) and consumed by
the import.

## Data

| What | Where |
| ---- | ----- |
| Skills (enabled) | `$DSH_HOME/skills/` |
| Skills (disabled) | `$DSH_HOME/skills-disabled/` |
| Import sources | other agent tool roots under `$HOME` (read-only) |

This package writes nothing else — no settings file, no patch layer edits. Its only dependency is
`node:` itself.

## Test

```bash
# from an installed copy (the host half resolves @deepseek-ai/* via the profile)
cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/plugins/dsh-skills"
node tests/skills.test.mjs
```

## License

MIT.

# dsh-zoom

Page zoom for the dsh web UI, with rebindable shortcuts.

Ported from DSHDesktop, where zoom was a native WebView2 `set_zoom` call plus a global keyboard hook.
Inside dsh there is no native window, so the zoom is CSS `zoom` on the page's document element and the
shortcuts are a capture-phase `keydown` listener. For dsh's own UI the result is the same; it just
cannot affect native window chrome (which does not exist here).

## Placement

With **[dsh-features](../dsh-features)** (the Features hub) installed, this panel appears on that hub's single
page and no longer docks its own corner button; without the hub (a bare dsh, or a profile where it is
not installed) the floating panel is built exactly as before. The coupling is two DOM-level
conventions (`window.__dshFeatures`, `#dsh-launchers`), described in the repository's AGENTS.md.

## Install

Installed straight from this repository, as a normal public package. `#path:` picks this package out
of the monorepo, since all seven live in one:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-zoom
# pin a commit:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#<sha>&path:/dsh-zoom
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-zoom
```

`--profile web` is DSHDesktop's shell, `--profile desktop` is the official desktop app; the panel
needs no flag. The pinned form is the reproducible one, and it is also how a fix reaches you: re-add
the spec with the newer commit.

In the desktop app, whose profile the command line cannot change, the same spec goes through its
**Plugins** page, **Add plugin**, which accepts a package name, a Git address or a local directory
path:

```text
github:LBurny/dsh-plugin#path:/dsh-zoom
```

Upgrading there is uninstall, then install the new version; the page has no auto-update, which is
what makes the pinned spec worth keeping. When GitHub is unreachable, retry with the page's
**Install source** choice: default, npm official, China mirror, or custom.

Restart dsh afterwards; plugins have no HMR. This package's browser half is served from disk on
every request, so a plain window reload is enough once dsh is up, and only a host-side change needs
the restart.

Two traps, both spelled out with their workarounds in the repository README. On Windows `dsh.cmd`
eats the `&` of the pinned form, so pin from the app's own page instead. And pnpm fetches with its
own TLS stack and ignores the system proxy, so a TLS-intercepting network needs `proxy=` and
`https-proxy=` lines in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/.npmrc`, or a fully offline install: copy the
package into `$DSH_HOME/profiles/plugins/dsh-zoom/` and add that path.

## What it does

- **Adjust** the zoom level with a slider, and the step size used by the shortcuts.
- **Rebind** either shortcut by pressing a key: click the keycap (or *Record*) and press the
  combination you want. Escape cancels a recording. A recording stays armed until a key arrives.
- **`/zoom`** prints the current level, the range and both shortcuts.
- **The level is capped by the window height.** `zoom` on `<html>` divides the layout viewport by the
  factor, so past `window height / ~360px` the harness's own sidebar is taller than its box and its
  bottom block (设置, 意见反馈, 退出登录) is clipped with nothing to scroll: the shell sets
  `overflow: hidden` and the document never scrolls. The panel shows the cap and the level is re-clamped
  when the window shrinks. `max` stays your preference; this bound is derived per window.
- **dsh's own popups stay put.** They are portaled to `<body>` and positioned from
  `getBoundingClientRect()`, which the zoom has already multiplied, so the factor used to land on their
  inline `top`/`left` a second time: at 110% the account menu fell below the avatar with its last row off
  the window. The stylesheet cancels the factor on those surfaces and re-applies it to their contents,
  which puts their coordinates back in the viewport space dsh's arithmetic actually assumes, so both the
  placement and the viewport clamp come out right. The card's own frame, its padding and the min/max
  width bounds, stays in viewport px, so a wide menu at a high zoom wraps a little tighter than a native
  page zoom would render it.

Shortcut matching prefers `event.code` and falls back to `event.key`, so synthesized and
remote-desktop key events still work.

## Routes

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| ------ | ---- | ------- |
| GET | `/dsh-zoom/panel.js` `/dsh-zoom/panel.css` | browser half |
| GET | `/dsh-zoom/api/settings` | current settings + the settings file path |
| POST | `/dsh-zoom/api/settings` | deep-merged settings patch |

## Data

| What | Where |
| ---- | ----- |
| Zoom level, step, bounds, both shortcuts, launcher on/off | `$DSH_HOME/dsh-zoom.json` |

This package touches nothing else: no patch layer edits, no skill directories.

## Test

```bash
cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/plugins/dsh-zoom"
node tests/zoom.test.mjs
```

## License

MIT.

# dsh-plugin

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Small independent [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) plugins: one feature per package, each installable on its own. ## Plugins

| Package | What it does | Command |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |
| `dsh-features` | The hub (Features): one sidebar entry between Plugins and Scheduled tasks, lists every installed feature plugin as a row like dsh's own Plugins page, opens one on click, reorders by drag. Install it to lose the floating corner buttons | |

| `dsh-doctor` | Harness diagnostics: version, port, pid, profile, log tail | `/doctor` |
| `dsh-zoom` | Page zoom with rebindable shortcuts | `/zoom` |
| `dsh-notify` | Task reminders: in-page popup, bundled sounds, browser notification | `/notify` |
| `dsh-remote` | Phone remote access: authenticated reverse proxy, QR link, optional Cloudflare tunnel, mobile UI rewrite, project browser | `/remote` |
| `dsh-init` | Write or update this workspace's `AGENTS.md`, the instruction file dsh loads into every session there | `/init` |
